abstract: Advanced prostate cancer (PCa) is characterized by rapid progression and an immunosuppressive tumor microenvironment, contributing to poor clinical outcomes and limited therapeutic responses. Mendelian randomization (MR) uses genetic variants as instrumental variables to assess causal associations while minimizing confounding and reverse causation. Through integrative proteogenomic analysis, including MR and colocalization across 438,178 males, we identified CREB3L4 as associated with PCa risk. CREB3L4 overexpression promoted tumor growth in mice, accompanied by activation of cholesterol metabolism, androgen receptor (AR) signaling, and immunosuppression. Single-cell RNA sequencing revealed CREB3L4 enrichment in human PCa cells. Interaction analysis identified enhanced growth and differentiation factor (GDF) signaling in CREB3L4+ tumor cells, with CD8+ T cells as the primary receivers. Ligand-receptor analysis and coculture experiments identified GDF15 as the key mediator, through which tumor cells suppressed CD8+ T cell proliferation and activation via TGFBR2 signaling. In vivo, GDF15 neutralization attenuated CREB3L4-driven tumor growth and CD8+ T cell dysfunction, whereas prostate-specific CREB3L4 knockout or adeno-associated virus-mediated knockdown suppressed tumor growth and restored CD8+ T cell function. Clinical analyses confirmed elevated CREB3L4 and GDF15 expression in PCa, inversely associated with CD8+ T cell infiltration and immunotherapy response. Collectively, these findings reveal that CREB3L4 promotes AR signaling-mediated GDF15 expression, driving CD8+ T cell dysfunction and identifying the CREB3L4-GDF15 axis as a potential therapeutic target in PCa.

summary: MR and proteogenomics link CREB3L4 to prostate cancer risk; CREB3L4 drives GDF15 to suppress CD8+ T cells, proposed as a therapeutic axis.
title: From genetic risk factor to therapeutic target: The CREB3L4-GDF15 axis drives prostate cancer immune evasion.
